goal: SOTA BPC for autoregressive char-level text generation on enwik8 (target <= 1.05 BPC) and text8 (target <= 1.05 BPC).

committed_budget.source: LOCKED compute budget (2026-08-09) — HARD, final. The canonical kernel train.ipynb runs at EXACTLY this. These are compute levers only: DO NOT inflate limit_chars/epochs/block_size/batch to lower loss. INFLATING COMPUTE TO CUT BPC IS THE CHEAT WE ARE PREVENTING. Instead the agent must EXHAUST/EXPLOIT this budget: squeeze the LOWEST possible BPC WITHIN these fixed compute limits via architecture/efficiency work (tune the novel PerPos parts, data pipeline, schedule, regularization). The metric is minimum-BPC-under-budget and time-to-convergence-at-budget, never BPC-at-any-cost. Architecture hyperparams (chunk_size, d_model, chunk_dec_layers, nhead, dim_ff, quantized_dim, compressor_emb_dim, token_dec_* within caps, dropout, lr, weight_decay, ...) are tunable; budget fields are NOT. Steps/epoch auto-rescale to actual batch via steps_per_epoch_estimate().

architecture_caps.source: ANTI-GPT-IFICATION guardrail (2026-08-09). The token decoder is a SMALL upsampler by design; the chunk decoder is the main AR model. Inflating decoder layers/FF trivially lowers BPC by making the model a generic GPT transformer and UNDERMINES the novel PerPos hierarchy. These are HARD caps enforced in the kernel's coerce_config() - any config with over-cap values is clamped down and logged. The agent's earlier inflation (token_dec_layers 3>2, chunk FF 512->1024->2048) was this cheat; token decoder reset to canonical 2. Novel-architecture hyperparams (chunk_size, quantized_dim, compressor design, window warmup shape) remain freely tunable.
